A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MotiF work. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human preference evaluations, automatic benchmark scores, and ablation experiments in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds qualitative examples for complex scenarios and an optical-flow throughput measurement.

M1.justification: The VideoCrafter2-based architecture, concatenated image conditioning, RAFT motion heatmaps, and combined diffusion and motion focal losses remain unchanged. The added computational details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 and Figure A2 add examples beyond TI2V-Bench covering object occlusion and multi-object interaction. The training dataset and evaluations on TI2V-Bench, Animate Bench, and VBench-I2V are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the nine-model human evaluation, Animate Bench results, and matched qualitative comparisons. VBench-I2V still compares MotiF with DynamiCrafter, Cinemo, and the static baseline. The new complex-scene examples show MotiF alone.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 replaces v1's explicit common 320×320 output resizing description with language about each method's optimal input aspect ratio and distortion-free outputs. This revises the reported preprocessing protocol; the PDFs do not establish that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure A2 adds four qualitative cases examining occlusion and object interaction. Existing loss, image-conditioning, SAM heatmap, and loss-weight ablations, the held-out loss analysis, and the original failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five annotators per comparison, majority voting, and the same justification-score aggregation. Neither introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing quantitative results in Figures 4 and 6 and Tables 2–4 and A1–A3 are unchanged, including the reported 72% average preference. v2 adds four complex-scene qualitative examples and optical-flow throughput of 2.1 videos per second.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses in Equations 1–3, heatmap normalization, and high-motion loss-ratio definition are retained. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim improved text and motion alignment through motion focal loss, introduce the 320-pair benchmark and human evaluation protocol, and report 72% average preference against nine models. The main contributions and their scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1 newly explains that optical-flow throughput remains constant for higher-resolution videos because frames are resized to 960×520. Existing motion-learning interpretations and failure limitations remain unchanged; the failure analysis is renumbered from C.2 to C.3.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.1 documents optical-flow speed on one Nvidia A100 and fixed 960×520 frame resizing. Section 5.2 removes the explicit 320×320 comparison resolution. Other training and inference details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 54 references and position loss-level motion guidance as complementary to existing conditioning techniques. The shortened related-work descriptions do not substantively change that positioning.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits and condenses the introduction and related work, standardizes TI2V Bench to TI2V-Bench, and adds and renumbers appendix subsections. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure A2 and renumbers the retained failure and evaluation-interface figures. Figure 3 and Table 1 move from page 6 to page 5, Table 4 is repositioned, and figure labels and spacing receive limited revisions.

improvement.justification: The added complex-scene examples and optical-flow cost and resizing details modestly improve the paper's evidence and implementation transparency while preserving its quantitative results and failure analysis. The gains are limited, and removing the explicit 320×320 comparison resolution leaves that protocol detail less precise.
